title: WPSB/202/2022 of DEVENDRA SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010101322022
2026:UHC:6958-DB
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Bench No. 399 of 2022
HON'BLE SRI MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
AND
HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE PANKAJ PUROHIT
06 August, 2026
Suvrata Prgaien ... Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand & others ... Respondents
With
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 202 of 2022
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. T.A. Khan, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Ms. Sheeba Ahmed,
with Mr. H.C. Joshi, learned counsel for the petitioners.
Mr. S.S. Chaudhary, learned Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned counsel for the respondent-Uttarakhand
Public Service Commission.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
(Per: Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
JUDGMENT
1. Since common questions of law and fact are
involved in both the petitions, therefore, they are being
heard and decided together. However, for the sake of
brevity and convenience, facts of WPSB No. 399 of
2022 alone are being considered and discussed.
2. Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (in
short 'Commission') issued advertisement dated
10.08.2021 inviting applications from eligible
candidates for Uttarakhand Combined State (Civil)
Upper Subordinate Service Examination-2021, for
appointment against vacancies available on various
posts. Out of the vacancies so notified, one vacancy
1

UKHC010101322022
2026:UHC:6958-DB
each was reserved for dependants of freedom fighters
(in short 'DFF') in the following posts (i) Finance
Officer, (ii) Block Development Officer & (iii) Deputy
Education Officer. Petitioner responded to the said
advertisement and claimed benefit available to DFF.
3. According to petitioner, in the admit card
issued to her, it was mentioned that she belongs to
Unreserved/Dependant of Freedom Fighter
(DFF)/Uttarakhand Female category; the preliminary
examination was held on 03.04.2022 and result thereof
was declared on 26.05.2022 and the same day, cut-off
mark for different categories was declared by another
notification, however, it was silent regarding cut-off
mark in respect of DFF. Petitioner contends that as per
the advertisement, reservation was available to DFF,
therefore, that benefit could not have been unilaterally
withdrawn or rules of game cannot be changed
midway, that too, without notice to the candidates.
4. In para 15 of the writ petition, it is mentioned
that there was no corrigendum issued by the
Commission regarding change in the number of
vacancies, reserved for dependants of freedom fighter,
therefore, Commission is bound to declare the result as
per the break-up of vacancies given in the
advertisement dated 10.08.2021.
5. Petitioner has challenged the result of
preliminary examination declared by Commission on
26.05.2022. She has also challenged the notice,
regarding cut-off mark for different categories, issued
2

UKHC010101322022
2026:UHC:6958-DB
by the Commission on 26.05.2022. The reliefs sought
in the writ petition are reproduced below for ready
reference:-
I. To issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
certiorari quashing the result declared by the respondent
no. 2 on 26-05-2022, bearing notice no. 27/01/PCS Pre-21/G-02/2022-23 (Annexure No. 1).
II. To issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
certiorari certiorari quashing of the notice of Cut off
Marks, bearing no. 27/03/PCS Pre-21/G-02/2022-23,
dated 26-05-2022 (Annexure No. 2) as well as the
amended notice of Cut off Marks bearing no. 29/03/PCS
Pre-21/G-02/2022-23, dated 30-05-2022 (Annexure No.
2).
III. To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus, commanding the respondents to declare the
results of the selected candidates of the category to the
Dependents of Freedom Fighters (DFF) in preliminary
examination in "Uttarakhand Combined State (Civil)
Upper Subordinate Service Examination-2021", in to the
pursuance advertisement bearing no. A-1/E-1/PCS-20-
21/21-22, dated 10-08-2021 (Annexure No. 3).
6. Petitioners had not qualified for appearing in
the mains examination. Coordinate Bench vide order
dated 29.07.2022 permitted them to participate in the
mains examination and pursuant to that order,
petitioners appeared in the mains examination.
7. As per counter affidavit filed on behalf of
Commission, pursuant to requisition sent by State
Government on 23.07.2021, selection was to be held
interalia for 18 posts of Finance Officer, 31 posts of
Deputy Education Officer and 28 posts of Block
Development Officer; one vacancy in each of the
aforesaid three posts was reserved for DFF, as per the
break-up given in the requisition and advertisement
was accordingly issued on 10.08.2021, strictly as per
3

UKHC010101322022
2026:UHC:6958-DB
the requisition; in that advertisement, it was mentioned
that number of vacancies are liable to be increased or
decreased; State Government thereafter re-determined
the vacancies and sent revised requisition on
04.10.2021, and as per the revised requisition, no
vacancy on the aforesaid three posts was reserved for
DFF. The corrigendum dated 07.12.2021, issued by
the Commission in terms of revised requisition is on
record as CA-2 to the counter affidavit filed by
Commission.
8. Learned counsel for the Commission submits
that corrigendum was published in all leading
newspapers for information to the candidates. It is
submitted that the allegation that rules of the game
were changed midway is not correct; original
advertisement was issued on 10.08.2021; corrigendum
was issued by the Commission on 07.12.2021;
preliminary examination was held on 03.04.2022 and
result of preliminary examination was declared on
26.05.2022. Thus, it is contended on behalf of
Commission that by means of corrigendum, everyone
was informed that the vacancy position, as indicated in
the advertisement dated 10.08.2021, has been altered
and petitioners could have challenged the corrigendum
before appearing in the preliminary examination, and
challenge thrown to the result of preliminary
examination is thus not sustainable.
9. Learned counsel for the Commission further
contended that Commission is a Selecting Body, which
holds selection strictly as per the requisition sent by
4

UKHC010101322022
2026:UHC:6958-DB
Government and the Recruitment Rules applicable for
the post, and whenever there is a doubt, Commission
has to seek clarification and act strictly as per the
instructions received from the Government, which is
the employer. He further submitted that DFF were
given relaxation in upper age limit upto five years,
therefore, in the admit card, issued to candidates
belonging to that category, DFF was mentioned.
10. Learned State Counsel submits that as per
the Government policy in vogue earlier, depending
upon number of vacancies, if share of any reserved
category in a post was '0.5' or more, then it was
treated as "1" and one vacancy was reserved for that
particular category; however, new policy was
introduced vide Government Order dated 22.05.2020,
but the reserved vacancies were determined in the
requisition dated 23.07.2021 as per old policy; this
mistake was rectified by issuing revised requisition to
the Commission on 04.10.2021. Learned State Counsel
further submits that revised requisition was sent within
less two months and selection had not progressed any
further during said period. Learned State Counsel
further submits that pursuant to revised requisition,
Commission issued corrigendum on 07.12.2021,
informing everyone that no vacancy is available to DFF
on the post of Finance Officer, Block Development
Officer and Deputy Education Officer.
11. Petitioners participated in the mains
examination on strength of interim order passed by this
Court. Their result was produced before us in a sealed
5

UKHC010101322022
2026:UHC:6958-DB
cover, which was opened in the presence of learned
counsel for the parties.
12. Perusal of the result reveals that petitioners
were treated as unreserved candidates and their score
of marks was less than the marks scored by last
General Category candidate who was declared
successful. The result further reveals that marks scored
by last successful General category candidate for the
post of Finance Officer, Block Development Officer and
Deputy Education Officer was 760, against which Ms.
Suvrata Pargaien scored 516 marks; Mr. Devendra
Singh scored 670 marks and Mr. Digambar Singh
scored 539 marks. Petitioner No. 3 (Mr. Surendra
Singh) in WPSB No. 202 of 2022 who applied for the
post of Assistant Director (Factory/Boiler) scored 913
marks as against 964 marks scored by last successful
General category candidate.
13. From the aforesaid discussion, it is apparent
that immediately after issuance of advertisement, in
terms of original requisition, State Government re-determined vacancies as per new policy which was
introduced on 22.05.2020 and sent a revised
requisition on 04.10.2021. Commission issued a
corrigendum in terms of revised requisition for
informing the candidates about change in vacancy
position and also alteration in the number of vacancies
available for different reserved categories. Thus,
petitioners cannot plead ignorance about the changes
brought about by the corrigendum. Thus, the
contention that rules of the game were changed
6

UKHC010101322022
2026:UHC:6958-DB
without notice after commencement of selection
process is factually incorrect.
14. It is not the case where vacancies reserved
for DFF were de-reserved without informing the
candidates. Here is a case where de-reservation of
vacancies by the State Government was duly notified to
the candidates by the Commission by issuing
corrigendum dated 07.12.2021.
15. Petitioner in WPSB No. 399 of 2022 has
challenged the result of preliminary examination and
also the notice issued by Commission, by which marks
scored by last successful candidate in different
categories was declared.
16. In WPSB No. 202 of 2022, petitioners
although have challenged corrigendum dated
07.12.2021 issued by Commission, however, the
grounds taken in the writ petition are not sufficient for
interfering with the corrigendum. Moreover, the State is
well within its right to correct the mistake in the
requisition and also to send revised requisition, if need
be.
17. In the advertisement dated 10.08.2021, it
was mentioned that number of vacancies may increase
or decrease. Petitioners cannot claim any vested right
of appointment based on vacancy position as indicated
in the advertisement.
18. While holding selection for appointment
under the State, Commission has to act as per the
7

UKHC010101322022
2026:UHC:6958-DB
applicable Recruitment Rules and the instructions
issued by State Government. Moreover, every selection
is to be made in terms of the break-up of vacancies
indicated in the requisition sent by State Government.
In such view of the matter, the Commission cannot be
faulted if there is alteration in vacancy position in the
corrigendum.
19. Petitioners have not challenged the revised
requisition issued by the Government on 04.10.2021,
which is the basis for issuing corrigendum dated
07.12.2021, therefore, there is no scope for
interference in the matter.
20. Learned counsel for Commission informed
that selection process concluded long back and selected
candidates are serving in different Departments since
last several years. None of the selected candidate is
before us. The relief, as claimed by petitioners, if
granted, will disturb the entire selection, thus affecting
rights of persons who are not party to these petitions.
21. For the aforesaid reasons, the writ petitions
fail and are dismissed. The result produced in Court in
a sealed cover, is resealed and returned to the learned
counsel for Commission.
_______________________________
MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, J.
____________________________
PANKAJ PUROHIT, J.
Dt: 06.08.2026
